purpose: Machine-facing educational KB for constructing portfolios and managing risk (asset allocation, MPT/efficient frontier, strategy selection, risk metrics, and risk control) as evaluable work units; it is educational and explicitly does NOT provide personalized investment advice and escalates personalized-advice requests for human judgment.
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
scope is educational portfolio/risk methodology, not personalized advice for any individual
a single subdomain node of a larger knowledge-searcher meta-KB
standard texts inform framing but are not used as measured data
exclusions: personalized allocation or buy/sell recommendations for a specific individual
live trade execution, order routing, and brokerage operations
single-security fundamental valuation and macro forecasting

competency_questions.question: Which portfolio/risk method family does this educational question require (allocation, optimization, risk measurement, control)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a scoped frame names the applicable method family

competency_questions.question: How do stated objectives, horizon, and constraints translate into educational risk bands and an IPS without becoming personal advice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: profile and IPS outputs are framed as educational and the advice boundary is enforced

competency_questions.question: What clean, aligned data and estimates are required before any optimization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a clean universe and a PSD covariance matrix exist with disclosed windows

competency_questions.question: How are systematic exposure (beta/factors) and risk-adjusted return measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: beta and Sharpe/Sortino are computed against disclosed benchmarks and windows

competency_questions.question: How is the efficient frontier built and validated for stability under estimation error?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: frontier and weights pass a stability/perturbation check

competency_questions.question: How is the strategic allocation chosen and reconciled with the investor's risk band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: allocation references the frontier and stays within the risk band

competency_questions.question: Passive vs active, rebalancing, and contribution timing: how are these implementation choices justified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: each choice is justified by cost, evidence, and drift control

competency_questions.question: How are fees, costs, and tax drag accounted for in net outcomes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: returns are reported net of fees, costs, and a generic tax-drag estimate

competency_questions.question: Which risk metrics, tail-risk estimates, and limits control downside?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: volatility, VaR/ES, drawdown, and concentration limits are defined

competency_questions.question: What data-governance and evidence-labeling rules apply to all estimates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: every estimate carries an evidence label and a source ref

competency_questions.question: How is overfitting and look-ahead bias controlled in estimation and backtesting?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: out-of-sample/walk-forward checks and disclosed controls are present

competency_questions.question: What ongoing monitoring detects breaches and triggers revisits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: every defined limit has a detection rule and a routed revisit action

competency_questions.question: In what order should the work proceed to minimize rework?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: priority_order respects dependencies and stabilizes foundations first

competency_questions.question: When must a request be escalated for human judgment instead of answered as education?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: any personalized-advice request is flagged and escalated

glossary.definition: set of portfolios with the highest expected return for each level of risk
combining low-correlation assets to reduce portfolio variance without proportionally reducing expected return
sensitivity of an asset or portfolio to market (benchmark) movements
excess return per unit of total volatility
threshold loss not expected to be exceeded at a given confidence over a horizon
average loss in the tail beyond the value-at-risk threshold
peak-to-trough decline in portfolio value over a period
restoring portfolio weights toward the policy allocation after drift
investing fixed amounts on a schedule regardless of price
long-run policy mix of asset classes that anchors the risk profile
determining how much capital to commit to each holding under concentration limits
document of objectives, constraints, and guardrails governing portfolio decisions

evidence_label_policy.rationale: no observed or experimental evidence supplied; all values are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR

source_registry.description: Model heuristic priors for portfolio construction and risk management, informed by standard texts (Malkiel; Bodie, Kane & Marcus) but not measured data.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Malkiel, A Random Walk Down Wall Street; Bodie, Kane & Marcus, Investments

nodes.definition: Bound the portfolio/risk work unit: state the educational objective, horizon, constraints, asset universe, and which allocation/risk methods apply.

excluded: personalized allocation recommendation for an individual

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: objective, horizon, or constraint set changes

pros.claim: scope fixes which risk/allocation methods are even applicable
pros.example: deciding a question is asset allocation, not single-stock valuation

cons.claim: over-scoping drags effort into non-applicable method families
cons.example: modeling factor tilts for a simple index-only educational question

failure_modes: mis-scoping the question as advice when it is educational
acceptance_tests: frame names objective, horizon, constraints, universe, method family, and the advice boundary

nodes.definition: Govern data sources and evidence labels for all return/risk estimates so heuristic priors are never overstated as observed.

excluded: claiming backtest as guaranteed future result

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a data source's freshness or eligibility changes

pros.claim: prevents heuristic estimates being mislabeled as measured fact
pros.example: flagging a 3-year backtest as heuristic, not a guarantee

cons.claim: strict labeling slows analysts who want quick point estimates
cons.example: blocking a Sharpe claim until the return window is disclosed

failure_modes: stale price data treated as current
acceptance_tests: every numeric estimate carries an evidence label and a source ref

nodes.definition: Translate stated goals, horizon, liquidity needs, and risk tolerance into educational portfolio constraints WITHOUT issuing personalized allocations.

excluded: recommending a specific allocation to a named individual

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stated goals, horizon, or tolerance change

pros.claim: grounds risk targets in objectives rather than arbitrary numbers
pros.example: mapping a long horizon to a higher equity-risk educational band

cons.claim: risk of crossing into personalized advice if applied to a specific person
cons.example: being asked 'what should I buy?' and needing to escalate

failure_modes: sliding from education into personalized advice
acceptance_tests: profile outputs are framed as educational bands and the advice boundary is enforced

nodes.definition: Define the candidate asset classes and instruments and assemble clean, aligned price/return series for analysis.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: universe membership or a data feed changes

pros.claim: clean aligned series are the substrate for all estimation
pros.example: aligning monthly total-return series across ETFs and bonds

cons.claim: survivorship and look-ahead bias silently corrupt the universe
cons.example: backfilling an index that dropped failed constituents

acceptance_tests: series are aligned in frequency, currency, and total-return basis

nodes.definition: Estimate expected returns, volatilities, and the covariance/correlation matrix that drive diversification and optimization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: estimation window, frequency, or shrinkage choice changes

pros.claim: correlation and covariance are what make diversification work
pros.example: low correlation between bonds and equities lowering portfolio variance

cons.claim: estimates are noisy and unstable; small input errors blow up optimizers
cons.example: a near-singular covariance matrix producing extreme weights

acceptance_tests: covariance matrix is positive semidefinite and shrinkage/window are disclosed
correlation assumptions stress-tested toward 1 in crisis

nodes.definition: Characterize systematic exposure: market beta (CAPM), factor tilts, and how exposures aggregate at the portfolio level.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark or factor definition changes

pros.claim: separates market-driven risk from asset-specific risk
pros.example: seeing a portfolio's beta is 1.2 so it amplifies market moves

cons.claim: beta is unstable and backward-looking
cons.example: a low historical beta that spikes in a drawdown

acceptance_tests: beta is estimated against a disclosed benchmark and its instability is noted

nodes.definition: Construct the efficient frontier and candidate optimal weights via mean-variance optimization under stated constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: input estimates or constraints change

pros.claim: formalizes the return-for-risk tradeoff into an efficient frontier
pros.example: showing the minimum variance achievable for a target return

cons.claim: optimizers maximize estimation error, producing fragile corner weights
cons.example: an unconstrained solve dumping 90% into one low-vol asset

acceptance_tests: weights respect all constraints and are stress-checked for stability under input perturbation
frontier is presented as estimate-dependent, not guaranteed

nodes.definition: Set the strategic (policy) allocation across asset classes that anchors diversification and the long-run risk profile.

excluded: personalized allocation for a named individual

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: policy weights or strategic assumptions change

pros.claim: allocation policy is the dominant driver of long-run risk and return
pros.example: a 60/40 policy anchoring the portfolio's risk level

cons.claim: a fixed policy can drift from objectives and crosses into advice if personalized
cons.example: an aggressive policy applied to a short-horizon need

acceptance_tests: allocation is diversified across low-correlation classes and stays within the educational risk band
output is framed as educational, not a personal recommendation

nodes.definition: Choose between passive (index) and active implementation given cost, evidence on manager skill, and tracking objectives.

excluded: picking specific winning managers with certainty

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cost or evidence-on-skill assumptions change

pros.claim: low-cost indexing reliably captures market return net of fees
pros.example: using a broad index fund instead of a high-fee active fund

cons.claim: active adds cost and manager risk with uncertain payoff
cons.example: paying for active management that underperforms its benchmark net of fees

failure_modes: fee drag from active without skill
acceptance_tests: each sleeve's passive/active choice is justified by cost and evidence on skill

nodes.definition: Design the contribution/funding schedule, including dollar-cost averaging versus lump-sum, as an educational tradeoff.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cash-flow profile or contribution policy changes

pros.claim: DCA reduces regret and smooths entry-timing risk behaviorally
pros.example: spreading a large deposit over several months

cons.claim: DCA can lag lump-sum in expectation when markets trend up
cons.example: holding cash that misses an early rally

acceptance_tests: schedule is presented as a behavioral/timing-risk tradeoff, not a return guarantee

nodes.definition: Translate target weights into position sizes with concentration limits so no single holding dominates portfolio risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: concentration policy or target weights change

pros.claim: caps limit the damage any single position can do to the portfolio
pros.example: capping any single stock at 5% of the portfolio

cons.claim: tight caps can force away from the optimized weights
cons.example: trimming a high-conviction holding to meet a cap

acceptance_tests: no position or correlated cluster exceeds its concentration limit

nodes.definition: Compute standard risk and risk-adjusted-return metrics: volatility, beta, Sharpe and Sortino ratios.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: risk-free rate, window, or benchmark changes

pros.claim: Sharpe makes returns comparable per unit of risk
pros.example: ranking two funds by return per unit of volatility

cons.claim: ratios assume stable distributions and mislead on fat tails
cons.example: a high Sharpe that hides large tail losses

acceptance_tests: metrics state their window, risk-free rate, and distributional assumptions

nodes.definition: Estimate downside and tail risk via value-at-risk, expected shortfall, and scenario stress tests.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scenario set or distributional assumptions change

pros.claim: quantifies plausible loss magnitudes beyond volatility
pros.example: estimating a 5% chance of losing more than 12% in a month

cons.claim: parametric VaR understates fat-tailed and correlated crash losses
cons.example: a Gaussian VaR missing a correlated crash

failure_modes: false comfort from a single VaR number
acceptance_tests: VaR is paired with expected shortfall and explicit stress scenarios
tail correlations stressed toward 1

nodes.definition: Analyze peak-to-trough drawdowns and define educational drawdown limits and de-risking triggers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: drawdown policy or risk band changes

pros.claim: drawdown limits address the loss path investors actually feel
pros.example: setting a 20% max-drawdown educational threshold

cons.claim: hard drawdown stops can lock in losses and miss recoveries
cons.example: de-risking at the bottom and missing the rebound

acceptance_tests: drawdown limits are framed with recovery-time context and as educational, not mechanical advice

nodes.definition: Define the rebalancing method (calendar or threshold bands) that restores the portfolio toward its policy allocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: drift bands, schedule, or cost assumptions change

pros.claim: rebalancing restores the intended risk profile and harvests a diversification premium
pros.example: selling outperformers to buy laggards back to policy weights

cons.claim: frequent rebalancing raises costs and taxes
cons.example: monthly rebalancing eroding returns via transaction costs

acceptance_tests: rebalancing trades only when drift exceeds bands and costs are accounted for

nodes.definition: Quantify the drag from fees, transaction costs, spreads, and taxes on net portfolio outcomes.

excluded: jurisdiction-specific tax optimization for an individual

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fee schedule, turnover, or tax context changes

pros.claim: costs compound and are one of the few reliably controllable variables
pros.example: a 1% fee compounding into a large lifetime drag

cons.claim: tax modeling is jurisdiction-specific and risks becoming personalized advice
cons.example: needing to escalate when asked about a specific tax situation

acceptance_tests: net returns are reported after fees, costs, and a generic tax-drag estimate

nodes.definition: Capture mandates, constraints, and an investment-policy-statement (IPS) structure that bounds all allocation and risk decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a mandate, exclusion, or constraint changes

pros.claim: an IPS keeps decisions disciplined and inside agreed limits
pros.example: an exclusion list keeping prohibited assets out of optimization

cons.claim: over-constraining can make the optimization infeasible
cons.example: constraints so tight no allocation satisfies them

acceptance_tests: all downstream weights satisfy the constraint set and exclusions

nodes.definition: Backtest the constructed portfolio and attribute realized risk and return to allocation, selection, and timing, with overfitting controls.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: backtest window, benchmark, or method changes

pros.claim: attribution shows whether risk and return came from allocation or selection
pros.example: attributing most return to the strategic allocation, not stock picking

cons.claim: backtests overfit and over-promise out-of-sample
cons.example: a tuned strategy that looks great in-sample and fails live

acceptance_tests: backtest uses out-of-sample/walk-forward checks and discloses look-ahead controls
results framed as past, not predictive of the future

nodes.definition: Operate the ongoing monitoring loop that watches drift, risk-limit breaches, and assumption changes and triggers revisits.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a monitored limit or assumption is breached

pros.claim: continuous monitoring catches drift and breaches before they compound
pros.example: an alert when an asset class drifts past its rebalancing band

cons.claim: alert fatigue and over-monitoring drive needless churn
cons.example: reacting to every minor fluctuation

acceptance_tests: every defined limit has a detection rule and a routed revisit action

nodes.definition: Synthesize the analysis into an educational portfolio decision package, explicitly flagging any personalized-advice request for human judgment.
inputs: allocation, strategy, risk, and cost outputs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any upstream output or the advice boundary status changes

pros.claim: synthesis turns analysis into a usable, bounded educational package
pros.example: delivering an allocation rationale plus an explicit 'not personal advice' note

cons.claim: synthesis can over-claim certainty or cross the advice boundary
cons.example: being pushed to say exactly what an individual should buy

acceptance_tests: package states it is educational and not personalized advice
every personalized-advice request is flagged for human judgment
all major tradeoffs are reconciled or escalated

nodes.definition: Run the validation and QA gate over estimates, weights, risk numbers, and the advice boundary before anything is locked.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any locked or high-coupling component changes

pros.claim: the QA gate blocks fragile weights and overstated risk numbers from locking
pros.example: stopping a lock when the covariance matrix is unstable

cons.claim: a heavy QA gate slows delivery
cons.example: blocking a decision package pending a recomputed VaR

acceptance_tests: all formula, bound, and reference checks pass and the advice boundary is audited before any hard lock

edges.why_related: Scope determines which data and evidence labels are needed.
edges.resolution_rule: scope decision dominates; relabel data if scope changes

edges.why_related: Scope frames the educational profiling task.
edges.example: profiling for a single person beyond educational scope
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; escalate if it becomes personalized

edges.why_related: Scope selects which asset classes enter the universe.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates universe membership

edges.why_related: Evidence rules govern which data is admissible into the universe.
edges.resolution_rule: evidence governance dominates; reject unlabeled data

edges.why_related: Profile objectives become formal constraints/IPS.
edges.resolution_rule: profile dominates; revise IPS when profile changes

edges.why_related: Estimation runs on the assembled return series.
edges.resolution_rule: fix the universe first; re-estimate

edges.why_related: Beta/factor exposure derives from return series and covariances.
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize estimation before factor analysis

edges.why_related: Optimization consumes the return vector and covariance matrix.
edges.resolution_rule: re-estimate and shrink before optimizing

edges.why_related: Risk metrics are computed from the estimated return/vol series.
edges.example: Sharpe from an unstable vol estimate
edges.resolution_rule: re-estimate before reporting metrics

edges.why_related: Tail-risk models use the covariance and return distribution.
edges.resolution_rule: extend/stress the estimation before VaR

edges.why_related: Profile risk band constrains the feasible optimization region.
edges.resolution_rule: risk band bounds the optimizer; clip to feasible set

edges.why_related: IPS constraints/exclusions limit admissible weights.
edges.resolution_rule: IPS constraints are hard bounds on the solve

edges.why_related: Strategic allocation is chosen from the frontier/candidate weights.
edges.example: policy far from any efficient point
edges.resolution_rule: allocation must reference the frontier; justify deviations

edges.why_related: Profile risk band bounds the strategic allocation.
edges.example: aggressive policy for a conservative band
edges.resolution_rule: band dominates; reduce risk to fit

edges.why_related: Implementation choice follows the policy allocation per sleeve.
edges.example: active bet inside a passive policy sleeve
edges.resolution_rule: allocation dominates; pick implementation per sleeve

edges.why_related: Contribution schedule funds the target allocation.
edges.resolution_rule: allocation dominates; contributions track policy weights

edges.why_related: Position sizes implement the allocation under concentration limits.
edges.resolution_rule: allocation weights dominate within concentration caps

edges.why_related: Rebalancing restores the portfolio to the policy allocation.
edges.resolution_rule: policy weights are the rebalance anchor

edges.why_related: Drawdown analysis builds on the return/vol metrics.
edges.resolution_rule: compute metrics first; then drawdowns

edges.why_related: Tail-risk estimates inform concentration and size limits.
edges.resolution_rule: tail risk tightens position caps

edges.why_related: Tail estimates shape drawdown limits and de-risk triggers.
edges.example: drawdown limit blind to tail risk
edges.resolution_rule: tail analysis informs drawdown thresholds

edges.why_related: Monitoring watches sized positions for limit breaches and triggers revisit of sizing.
edges.example: a position drifting past its cap unnoticed
edges.resolution_rule: on breach, revisit POSITION_SIZING; stop when within limits

edges.why_related: Monitoring tracks drawdowns and triggers de-risk review.
edges.resolution_rule: on limit breach, revisit drawdown policy; stop when recovered

edges.why_related: Monitoring detects drift and triggers rebalancing review.
edges.resolution_rule: on band breach, trigger rebalance review; stop within bands

edges.why_related: The allocation is what gets backtested and attributed.
edges.resolution_rule: backtest the current allocation; re-run on change

edges.why_related: Monitoring breaches can trigger revisit of the strategic allocation.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit allocation only on material, persistent breaches; stop when realigned

edges.why_related: Backtest evidence can prompt revisiting the allocation, risking overfitting.
edges.example: tweaking weights to fit past data
edges.resolution_rule: require out-of-sample support before changing allocation; cap iterations

edges.why_related: The decision package is built on the strategic allocation.
edges.resolution_rule: allocation must be settled before synthesis

edges.why_related: Sized positions and limits enter the decision package.
edges.resolution_rule: include concentration limits in synthesis

edges.why_related: Tail-risk numbers must appear in the decision package.
edges.resolution_rule: include VaR/ES and stress results in synthesis

edges.why_related: The package must pass the QA gate before any lock.
edges.resolution_rule: QA gate must pass before lock

edges.why_related: Optimized weights are validated for stability and constraints.
edges.resolution_rule: validate weight stability before acceptance

edges.why_related: Estimates are validated (PSD, window disclosure) at the gate.
edges.resolution_rule: validate estimates before downstream lock

edges.why_related: Optimizer-optimal weights conflict with diversified, robust policy weights.
edges.risk_of_conflict: fragile corner solution adopted as policy
edges.example: an unconstrained optimum that is dangerously concentrated
edges.resolution_rule: prefer robust diversified policy over fragile optimum; constrain the solve

edges.why_related: Active strategy's potential edge conflicts with its higher cost.
edges.risk_of_conflict: paying for active that fails net of fees
edges.example: an active fund underperforming after fees
edges.resolution_rule: require net-of-cost evidence; default to low-cost passive when unproven

edges.why_related: Volatility-based metrics understate fat-tailed risk captured by tail models.
edges.example: a high Sharpe masking large tail loss
edges.resolution_rule: tail risk dominates for downside decisions; pair both

edges.why_related: DCA cash holding conflicts with being fully invested at policy weights.
edges.risk_of_conflict: large cash drag from slow DCA
edges.example: months of uninvested cash missing returns
edges.resolution_rule: frame as a behavioral timing-risk tradeoff; bound the DCA horizon

edges.why_related: Tighter rebalancing reduces drift but raises cost and tax drag.
edges.resolution_rule: use threshold bands so trades only fire on material drift

edges.why_related: Pressure to give a personal answer conflicts with the educational advice boundary.
edges.example: being pushed to recommend exact buys for a person
edges.resolution_rule: advice boundary dominates; escalate personalized requests to human judgment

conflict_axes.trigger: the unconstrained optimum is concentrated/fragile while the robust policy is diversified
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: robust diversified policy dominates a fragile optimum; constrain and stability-test the solve
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: weights flip materially under small input perturbations
conflict_axes.example: an unconstrained solve placing 80% in one asset

conflict_axes.trigger: active management promises an edge but adds fees and turnover
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: default to low-cost passive unless net-of-cost evidence supports active
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: active underperforms its benchmark net of fees
conflict_axes.example: a high-fee active fund trailing a cheap index fund

conflict_axes.trigger: Sharpe/volatility look good while fat-tail risk is high
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tail risk dominates downside decisions; always pair volatility metrics with VaR/ES and stress tests
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a high Sharpe coincides with a large stress-test loss
conflict_axes.example: a strategy with a great Sharpe that crashes in a correlated selloff

conflict_axes.trigger: tighter rebalancing reduces drift but raises trading and tax cost
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: use threshold bands so trades fire only on material drift; cost-benefit must be positive
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: monthly rebalancing erodes net return for tiny drift
conflict_axes.example: frequent small trades whose costs exceed the drift benefit

conflict_axes.trigger: spreading contributions reduces entry-timing regret but holds uninvested cash
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: frame as a behavioral timing-risk tradeoff; bound the DCA horizon to limit cash drag
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: months of cash miss a rally
conflict_axes.example: a slow DCA leaving most capital uninvested during a rising market

conflict_axes.trigger: concentration caps force deviation from optimized weights
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: concentration caps dominate; accept a small efficiency loss for bounded single-name risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a cap trims a high-weight optimizer pick
conflict_axes.example: reducing an 18% optimizer weight to a 5% cap

conflict_axes.trigger: a decision package could ship before estimates and weights are validated
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation dominates speed for high-risk nodes; no hard lock before QA passes
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: shipping a package with an unvalidated covariance matrix
conflict_axes.example: locking weights before a stability check

conflict_axes.trigger: a user asks for a specific personal allocation or buy/sell recommendation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the educational advice boundary dominates; personalized-advice requests are escalated to human judgment, never answered as a recommendation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: being asked exactly what to buy with a given sum
conflict_axes.example: a request for a personal allocation for a named individual

edge_cases.example: optimizer produces extreme unstable weights case
edge_cases.detection_method: check matrix is positive semidefinite; test weight stability under input perturbation
resolution: apply shrinkage to the covariance matrix

edge_cases.failure_mode: overstated historical returns and understated risk
edge_cases.example: overstated historical returns and understated risk case
edge_cases.detection_method: audit universe construction for delisted names and point-in-time membership

edge_cases.example: great in-sample results fail out-of-sample case
edge_cases.detection_method: run walk-forward/out-of-sample tests and compare in- vs out-of-sample metrics
compare parametric VaR with historical/expected-shortfall and stress scenarios

edge_cases.trigger: diversified names that are highly correlated
edge_cases.example: effective concentration despite many holdings case
edge_cases.detection_method: measure correlation clusters and effective number of bets, not just count of holdings

edge_cases.trigger: user requests a personalized buy/sell or allocation
edge_cases.failure_mode: crossing from education into unlicensed personal advice
edge_cases.example: crossing from education into unlicensed personal advice case
edge_cases.detection_method: scan requests for personalization cues (a named person, a specific sum, 'should I')

edge_cases.trigger: stale risk-free rate or mismatched estimation window
edge_cases.example: Sharpe/beta computed on inconsistent inputs case
edge_cases.detection_method: assert risk-free rate and window match across metrics and are disclosed

edge_cases.failure_mode: cost and tax drag exceed the drift benefit
edge_cases.example: cost and tax drag exceed the drift benefit case
edge_cases.detection_method: compare rebalancing cost against the drift it corrects

edge_cases.trigger: heuristic/backtest result labeled as observed or guaranteed
edge_cases.example: overstated certainty in the package case
edge_cases.detection_method: audit evidence labels against source eligibility (no observed without data)

edge_cases.failure_mode: no allocation satisfies the constraint set
edge_cases.example: no allocation satisfies the constraint set case
edge_cases.detection_method: check optimizer feasibility against the constraint set before solving

edge_cases.trigger: a tradeoff modeled as a dependency instead of a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: priority order and dominance logic corrupted
edge_cases.example: priority order and dominance logic corrupted case
edge_cases.detection_method: verify conflict edges carry negative signed_tension and resolution rules, not dependency semantics

edge_cases.trigger: monitoring runs on an unvalidated or stale baseline
edge_cases.failure_mode: breaches missed or false alerts churn the portfolio
edge_cases.example: breaches missed or false alerts churn the portfolio case
edge_cases.detection_method: ensure only validated outputs feed monitoring and assumptions are time-stamped

workflow.objective: assemble the educational decision package and enforce the advice boundary

priority_rationale.notes: root frame; selects method families and the advice boundary
governs data admissibility before any estimation
objectives drive risk bands and the advice boundary
clean data is the substrate for estimation

dominance_rules.trigger: a personalized buy/sell or allocation is requested
dominance_rules.rule: the educational advice boundary dominates the urge to give a personal answer
dominance_rules.required_action: flag the request and escalate to human judgment; return educational framing only
dominance_rules.example: refusing to name an exact allocation for an individual and escalating

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk node could be finalized quickly without checks
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk_if_wrong nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before finalizing
dominance_rules.example: blocking a decision package until the covariance matrix is validated

dominance_rules.rule: robust diversified policy dominates a fragile optimum
dominance_rules.required_action: constrain and stability-test the solve; prefer diversified weights
dominance_rules.example: rejecting an 80%-in-one-asset optimum for a diversified policy

dominance_rules.trigger: downside decisions rely only on volatility metrics
dominance_rules.rule: tail risk dominates volatility metrics for downside control
dominance_rules.required_action: pair every volatility metric with VaR/ES and stress tests
dominance_rules.example: overriding a high Sharpe when stress tests show large losses

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks its prerequisites
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule prerequisites first even if a later node has higher value
dominance_rules.example: estimating covariance before optimizing despite optimization being high-value

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic and cite SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR
dominance_rules.example: labeling a backtest Sharpe as heuristic, not observed

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is proposed for hard lock before QA
dominance_rules.required_action: no hard lock before formula, reference, and advice-boundary checks pass
dominance_rules.example: keeping weights in draft until the QA gate passes

dominance_rules.required_action: treat constraints/exclusions as hard bounds on the solve
dominance_rules.example: excluding a prohibited asset the optimizer wanted to hold

dominance_rules.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses the review threshold
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation above thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off for risk>=0.80 or irreversible commitments
dominance_rules.example: human review before treating an allocation as final

dominance_rules.trigger: active management is chosen without net-of-cost evidence
dominance_rules.rule: cost-justified default to passive dominates unproven active
dominance_rules.required_action: require net-of-cost evidence before selecting active
dominance_rules.example: defaulting to a low-cost index fund absent active-skill evidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not analyze before scope, constraints, and the advice boundary are fixed
anti_rework_rules.rationale: wrong-scope or advice-crossing work is total rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: analysis exists with no scoped frame or advice-boundary flag
anti_rework_rules.example: building an allocation for an out-of-scope, personalized question

anti_rework_rules.rule: define evidence governance before assigning any labels
anti_rework_rules.rationale: relabeling every estimate later is expensive
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an estimate carries a label with no governing rule
anti_rework_rules.example: labeling Sharpe observed before evidence rules exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: clean and align the universe before estimating
anti_rework_rules.rationale: estimation on dirty data is discarded
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: estimates computed on misaligned or biased series

anti_rework_rules.rationale: optimizing on bad inputs maximizes error
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: weights solved from a non-PSD matrix
anti_rework_rules.example: frontier built before the matrix is checked PSD

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the strategic allocation before implementation and sizing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sizing and strategy choices made before allocation are redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: positions sized with no settled allocation
anti_rework_rules.example: sizing positions before the policy mix is chosen

anti_rework_rules.rationale: a package without tail risk must be rebuilt

anti_rework_rules.rule: compute net-of-cost figures before the decision package
anti_rework_rules.rationale: gross-only packages mislead and get redone
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming returns without fees and tax drag

anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking a defective artifact forces a downgrade and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard_lock with no passing validation report
anti_rework_rules.example: locking weights before the formula checks pass

anti_rework_rules.rationale: monitoring an unvalidated state produces false signals
anti_rework_rules.example: alerting on metrics that failed QA

anti_rework_rules.rule: map conflicts before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules without mapped conflicts are incomplete
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a dominance rule with no corresponding conflict axis
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a resolution rule for an unmapped tradeoff

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation or formula check fails
action: route each to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: every failed check has an owner

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream coupling
action: score defects by risk_if_wrong and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-coupling or locked component changed
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges of the changed node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change are identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to its repair subsystem
action: apply the formula/reference/evidence fix in the owning subsystem
acceptance_tests: the targeted check now passes
no new failures introduced and the target check passes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes or only sub-threshold warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a regime shift occurs
iteration_protocol.detection: posterior delta exceeds the revisit threshold
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed from explicit inputs only
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior delta below the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream input to a locked artifact changed materially
iteration_protocol.detection: compare the new input against the locked assumption
acceptance_tests: no stale hard_lock remains over a changed input
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all affected locks downgraded and revalidated

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk crosses a threshold or a personalized-advice request appears
iteration_protocol.detection: risk>=0.80, irreversibility high, or advice-boundary trigger
action: route to human review with a decision record
acceptance_tests: a human decision record exists before finalizing
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human sign-off recorded or the request is declined as out of scope

user asks what they personally should buy

version_increment_rules: increment on any change to a hard_locked figure
increment when a method family is added or removed
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade to draft when an upstream input changes materially
downgrade and revalidate when a formula or constraint changes
